Maya: Heads up — saw a repeating "eviction stutter" pattern on qwen-34b-mqa during a long chat loadtest. Memory climbs steadily, then a ~200ms latency spike + eviction burst, then memory drops ~200MB, then it climbs again. Repro on rope-scaled prefixes > 64k tokens.
PerfBot: ALERT: high-kv-evict-rate detected on node gpu-12 (2959994300) :eyes:
Trent: Do we have profiler + kernel switch logs for that window?
Maya: Yep, pushing the short trace below. It lines up with a kernel fallback at 2959994318.
Maya: ```
# rb-kv-profiler summary (2959994300-2959994330)
kv_total_pages: 18236
evict_ops: 112
evict_latency_p95_ms: 198
kernel_switches: 1 -> fallback_kernel (mqa->gqa_compat)
page_frag_ratio: 0.42
prefix_len_avg: 78k
```
Liam: Interesting — kernel selection log shows a selective switch due to a sequence-length heuristic. When batcher sees mixed seq-lens it picks gqa_compat kernel to avoid MQA oversharding. That kernel does slightly different slab alignment which increases fragmentation.
Liam: log excerpt: `kernel_select: prefer=mqa if uniform_seqlen else gqa_compat (score_delta=0.13) -> selected=gqa_compat`
Anika: So the sequence-length router + batching heuristic is oscillating under that load, causing a cross-kernel page layout mismatch. Eviction then reclaims pages but new allocations come with different slab offsets -> fragmentation + repeated small evicts.
Trent: Any model-specific signals? Is qwen's kv slot size different for MQA vs GQA variants?
Maya: Yes. Qwen-MQA uses 128B kv slot packing; GQA_compat path falls back to 256B-aligned pages for compatibility. That mismatch is the crux.
Anika: Proposed short mitigations: 1) pin kernel for sessions whose prefix > 32k tokens (prefer MQA kernel if initially chosen) 2) add a soft batching guard to avoid mixing very long prefixes with short ones in same micro-batch 3) opportunistic KV defrag during low load windows.
Liam: Agreed. Also a profiling tweak: add per-kernel page-signature in the allocator so we can detect cross-kernel page churn without heavy traces. Cheap checksum per page.
Trent: Can we craft a runbook for on-call? Quick steps: check perfbot, confirm kernel switch, look at kv page_frag_ratio, then run temporary kernel_pin on the node.
Maya: Draft runbook snippet: ```
1) perfbot alerts -> open thread
2) ssh gpu node -> /opt/redwood/bin/kernel-log --since=5m
3) rb-kv-stats --json | jq .page_frag_ratio
4) if page_frag_ratio > 0.35 and kernel_switches>0: rb-kernel-pin --session <sid> --kernel mqa
5) schedule defrag: rb-kv-defrag --max-delta 100MB
```
Trent: Good. Can we also add a telemetry flag to mark sessions that experienced a kernel fallback so we can correlate user-visible latency?
Anika: I'll add a short PR to tag session metadata and emit a metric kv.kernel_fallback{model,qwen_variant}.
Maya: Running a canary now on dedicated pool with kernel_pin enabled for qwen-mqa long sessions. Will post results.
PerfBot: NOTE: Canary started on pool dedicated-shard-7 at 2959994490
Liam: If canary looks good, let's schedule a conservative rollout and a longer-term fix: unify allocator alignment between kernels or add cross-kernel compatibility layer so pages are interchangeable.
Maya: TL;DR: root cause = batching heuristic + kernel selection -> cross-kernel slab alignment mismatch -> fragmentation -> eviction stutter under long prefixes. Mitigation = kernel pin + batching guard + short-term defrag; long-term = allocator unification. I'll follow up with concrete numbers after the canary. :thumbsup:
